sources.title: SphereFace Models | yakhyo/face-recognition | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: This document provides detailed technical documentation of the SphereFace model architectures available in this face recognition framework. SphereFace models are server-oriented neural networks designed for high-accuracy face recognition tasks where computational resources are less constrained compared to mobile deployments.

sources.title: SphereFace: Deep Hypersphere Embedding for Face Recognition
sources.snippet: This paper addresses deep face recognition (FR) problem under open-set protocol, where ideal face features are expected to have smaller maximal intra-class distance than minimal inter-class distance under a suitably chosen metric space. sources.title: SphereFace: Deep Hypersphere Embedding for Face Recognition
sources.snippet: Most of the existing face verification systems achieve high performance with huge training data or model ensemble. While using single model trained on publicly available dataset (CAISA-WebFace, relatively small and having noisy labels), SphereFace achieves 99.42% and 95.0% accuracies on LFW and YTF datasets.

sources.snippet: This page introduces the SphereFace repository, its research purpose, the A-Softmax loss function, published benchmark results, and the three-stage pipeline that makes up the codebase. For installation steps see Installation and Setup. For a deeper walkthrough of each pipeline stage see The SphereFace Pipeline. For the A-Softmax loss implementation see SphereFace Model and A-Softmax Loss.
